chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever emancipates a man as a Sa'ibah, there is nothing upon him from his crimes, and there is nothing for him from his inheritance, and let him bear witness to that.

key_terms.سَائِبَة: An unconditionally freed slave who is not bound by a specific period or condition of servitude.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling regarding the debts, crimes, and inheritance of an unconditionally freed slave (Sa'ibah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific legal status of a 'Sa'ibah'—a slave freed unconditionally without a defined price or period—establishing that the emancipator bears no liability for the freed slave's debts or crimes, nor does the slave inherit from the master. The requirement for witnesses underscores the importance of formal documentation in Shia jurisprudence to prevent disputes over this unique category of manumission. This ruling distinguishes the Sa'ibah from other forms of freed slaves, highlighting the precision of Imami legal theory regarding property and kinship rights.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The one emancipates a man unconditionally, so there is nothing upon him from his crimes, anything, and there is nothing for him from his inheritance, anything, and let him have witnesses upon that’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one frees a slave by manner of Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave) he is not liable for his crimes and there is nothing for him from his legacy and he must arrange witnesses for it.’”
